comment: Golden vectors for firmware-telemetry/v2 How Old A Reading Is, at the signing runtime. Each case runs its events in order, on a clock that counts suspended time, in nanoseconds, under the case's per-device and total table bounds. Every accept event is a message already accepted under every check; the corpus does not exercise verification. A conforming runtime reproduces every query's 'expected'. Nonces are fixed fixture values.

event_kinds.sign_liveness: the runtime signs a v 2 liveness message; t_ns is its signing start, or null when the clock could not be read
event_kinds.sign_liveness_v1: the runtime signs a v 1 liveness message, which carries no nonce and records nothing
event_kinds.sign_failed: the runtime begins signing a v 2 liveness message at t_ns and the signing fails; its entry is discarded and nothing is published
event_kinds.accept: the runtime accepts an envelope; channels lists its readings' channels, empty for a heartbeat
event_kinds.store_restore: the runtime's state store is restored while it runs
event_kinds.suspend: the host is suspended from t_ns until resume_t_ns
event_kinds.query: the bound of a message, or of a channel's latest reading, at t_ns

cases.name: matched_and_growing
cases.note: the bound is computed at use and grows after receipt

cases.name: rounds_up
cases.note: 2500001 ns is shown as 3 ms, never 2

cases.name: unknown_nonce
cases.note: a nonce the runtime never signed bounds nothing

cases.name: null_nonce
cases.note: a reading measured while the device held no nonce has no bound

cases.name: v1_envelope
cases.note: a v 1 envelope carries no nonce and has no bound

cases.name: other_device
cases.note: an entry matches only the device it was signed for

cases.name: other_boot
cases.note: an entry matches only the boot it was signed for

cases.name: other_manifest
cases.note: an entry matches only the manifest it was signed for

cases.name: accepted_exactly_an_hour_after_signing
cases.note: an entry still serves a lookup exactly one hour after its signing start

cases.name: accepted_past_the_hour
cases.note: one nanosecond later the entry no longer serves one

cases.name: matched_reading_older_than_an_hour
cases.note: the hour limits matching, not age: a matched reading keeps its signing start

cases.name: per_device_eviction
cases.note: the third entry for a device with room for two evicts its earliest

cases.name: total_eviction
cases.note: with room for two in total, the third entry evicts the table's earliest, another device's

cases.name: eviction_tie_goes_to_first_nonce_in_byte_order
cases.note: two entries share a signing start; the one whose nonce sorts first in byte order is evicted

cases.name: hour_old_entry_survives_a_recording_with_room
cases.note: recording another entry exactly an hour after the first, with room to spare, does not expire the first: its age is exactly one hour, which is still usable

cases.name: per_device_bound_before_total_bound
cases.note: the per-device bound is applied first: it evicts Y1, after which the table is under its total bound, so the other device's earlier X1 survives

cases.name: per_device_bound_spans_boots
cases.note: the per-device bound counts every entry for the device_id, whatever its boot_id: the third entry evicts the earlier boot's

cases.name: entry_at_the_hour_still_counts
cases.note: at exactly one hour the first entry is still usable and still counts, so recording a third evicts it: size eviction removes a usable entry

cases.name: rollout_failed_v2_signing_leaves_no_entry
cases.note: the interval's v 1 message is published; its v 2 signing fails and leaves no entry, so the device holds no nonce and a nonce from the failed signing matches nothing

cases.name: failed_signing_eviction_stands
cases.note: recording the failed signing's entry evicted the earliest; discarding it does not restore what it evicted

cases.name: rollout_reading_after_pair_bounded_by_v2
cases.note: a reading measured after the device accepted the pair carries the v 2 nonce and is bounded by its signing start

cases.name: rollout_reading_between_pair_unbounded
cases.note: a reading measured after the device accepted the v 1 message and before the v 2 message carries null and has no bound

cases.name: restart_before_acceptance
cases.note: a restart empties the table

cases.name: restart_after_acceptance
cases.note: a restart drops the signing start held with an accepted message; the stored reading has no bound and the channel has no latest reading

cases.name: live_store_restore_reissues_runtime_seq
cases.note: a store restore while the runtime runs reissues runtime_seq 5 under a fresh nonce; the device refuses it and keeps signing the first nonce, which the table still dates by its own signing start

cases.name: restart_and_restore_reissue_with_fresh_nonce
cases.note: after a restart and a restore, runtime_seq 5 is reissued under nonce B; an old reading carrying nonce A has no bound, where a bound keyed by runtime_seq would date it by B's signing; the next runtime_seq the device accepts bounds again

cases.name: heartbeat_does_not_refresh_channel
cases.note: the channel's latest reading is still the reading; the heartbeat's own bound is newer and says nothing about the channel

cases.name: unclocked_signing
cases.note: a signing whose start could not be read records no entry

cases.name: suspended_time_counts
cases.note: the clock counts the thirty minutes the host was suspended, so the bound includes them

cases.name: drained_backlog
cases.note: readings polled under older nonces and delivered together after an outage are each bounded by the nonce they were measured under
